<p class="page-deck">An interactive place-based atlas estimating benefits and costs of climate action for more than 46,000 UK communities across eleven benefit and cost categories.</p>

**Status:** Active<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Foundational Prior Work — Developed through the University of Edinburgh and collaborators before the lab was established at SFU; it is foundational rather than an SFU lab output.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

## How this project contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Where New Evidence Matters](/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html), [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

**Decision or problem:** How place-based evidence can make locally varying benefits and costs of climate action visible.

**Existing evidence:** Verified atlas methods, outputs and a connected publication from foundational prior work.

**Transfer conditions:** Estimates are specific to UK data, communities, scenarios and valuation choices.

**Consequential uncertainty:** Data availability and modelling choices affect which consequences can be represented at community scale.

**Consequences examined:** Eleven categories of benefits and costs across more than 46,000 UK communities.

**Evidence status:** Active foundational prior work with authoritative project and tool sources.

**Claim boundaries:** Atlas estimates are not universal predictions and do not establish suitability for another place.

**Next learning question:** Which additional local evidence would most improve interpretation of community-level differences?

### Research facets

**Geographies:** united-kingdom<br>

**Sectors:** cross-sectoral<br>

## Research questions

- How do the benefits and costs of climate action vary between UK communities?
- How can place-based evidence make local climate choices more transparent?
